decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approaches to the two rear white supports; keep both grippers open and separated.
Align open grippers with the rear support long axes, advancing cautiously; wrist views will determine final centering and depth.
Refine rear-block alignment from wrist images and lower to grasp height; no closure until centered.
Center the two rear supports between the fingers, then close both grippers. Retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Lift both closed grasps vertically to verify retention before transporting the base supports.
Both supports remained between the fingers on lifting. Transport them above symmetric base locations and straighten their yaw while keeping them upright.
Lower the retained base supports vertically to table height at symmetric positions, preserving upright alignment.
Release the two base supports at table height, then withdraw vertically to inspect stability before handling the lower board.
The released supports remain upright. Withdraw outward and rotate the empty wrists toward a two-ended grasp of the long lower board.
Complete the opposing wrist orientations and lower the open fingers above each end of the long board, using wrist images for the final approach.
Descend to the board edges with opposing level grasps, then close both grippers. Check retention before translating toward the supports.
Settle the two-ended grasp and lift the lower board evenly, keeping both grippers closed and their separation fixed.
The board lifted with both hands. Translate it level toward the two upright supports, retaining clearance above them.
Lower the centered board slowly onto both base supports, maintaining equal hand height and fixed separation.
Open both grippers to leave the lower board on the supports, then withdraw outward and upward without disturbing it.
The lower board remains supported after release. Move each empty hand outward toward its remaining white support, aligning to each block's yaw.
Approach the remaining supports more closely, refining yaw from the wrist views. Keep the fingers open until final centering is visible.
Use the closer wrist views to center each support laterally and align its long axis while descending to grasp height.
Correct fore-aft centering at grasp height: left slightly back, right forward. Keep both grippers open while resolving the wrist-view offsets.
The remaining supports are centered between the fingers. Make small final corrections, close both grasps, and lift slightly to check retention.
Both supports lifted in the grasps. Raise them above the lower board and begin moving inward while straightening their yaw.
Carry the retained supports above symmetric middle-layer positions, keeping them upright and clear of the lower board.
Lower the upright middle supports gently onto the completed lower board at equal, symmetric positions.
Release the middle supports on the lower board and withdraw both empty hands upward and outward before approaching the middle board.
The middle supports remain upright. Rotate the empty hands to opposing board grasps while moving back toward the shorter board.
Replan from the interrupted pose with much smaller wrist increments, completing the opposing orientations above the middle board.
Lower to the shorter board's grasp edges and close both grippers evenly, preserving opposing wrist alignment.
Lift the shorter board evenly above the middle supports, keeping both grippers closed and their relative pose fixed.
The middle board is retained in both hands. Carry it level over the two middle supports, preserving clearance and centering.
Lower the middle board evenly onto the two upright middle supports with small vertical increments.
Release the middle board on its supports and retreat outward and upward to verify stability before placing the top pieces.
The middle layer remains stable. Approach the small tan top board with the left hand and move the right hand outside the green top piece, keeping clear of the tower.
Complete the left wrist's approach orientation over the tan top board and refine the right hand's position over the green piece; both grasps remain open.
Refine the tan board's yaw and fore-aft centering while lowering; bring the open right gripper down around the green piece.
Correct fore-aft alignment of both top pieces at grasp height and remove small yaw errors; keep both grippers open for visual confirmation.
Both top pieces are centered in the wrist views. Close the two grasps and lift slightly to verify retention before moving toward the tower.
Both top pieces lifted with the grippers. Raise them above the tower, turning the tan board horizontally while keeping the green piece safely to the right.
Carry the tan board above the center of the middle layer and finish aligning its long axis. Hold the green piece stationary off to the right.
Make a small centering correction and lower the tan top board onto the middle board. Keep the green piece held clear to the right.
Release the centered tan board and withdraw the left gripper clear of the tower. Keep the green piece securely held in the right workspace.
The tan board remains centered after release. Move the retained green piece above it while withdrawing the left arm farther into its own workspace.
Correct the green piece's visible rightward offset and lower it toward the tan board. Begin a gradual left-arm return outside the tower.
Make a small final centering correction, release the green piece on the tan board, and withdraw the right fingers. Continue the gradual left-arm return.
All pieces remain upright after releasing the green top. Return the left arm toward origin and clear the right fingers before rotating the right arm away from the tower.
Keep the tower undisturbed with both grippers open. Settle the left arm at origin and continue the right arm's gradual elbow-up return.
Complete the right arm's smooth return to origin with both grippers open; the assembled tower remains upright and clear of the arms.
